packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-09 - unverified image-only reading

EXPOSURE / RULES
No proposed identification or prior reading was present in my context. I opened only PROMPT.md and the two image files of this packet. No web, search, catalogue or edition was used.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
Two images of ONE face only: image-001 = reduced overview with a grey scale and mm rule; image-002 = native-resolution view of the same face. No image of the other face is in the packet.
The fragment is a small, roughly square scrap (about 4 x 4 cm by the mm rule) of cream-coloured, fairly thick, fibrous material (it looks like paper rather than parchment - tentative), torn irregularly at the left and bottom, with holes; a strip of modern white repair tissue projects from the right edge. A vertical fold or ruling runs at about one quarter in from the right edge, and another near the left edge.
Orientation: text upright. The top c. 30% is blank (upper margin). The right c. 40% is blank (margin or intercolumn; the line ends form a fairly even right boundary, so this is the right edge of a text block). Nine short lines of a small, rapid, extremely abbreviated cursive in brown ink survive, each cut at the left by the tear, so the fragment gives LINE ENDS: the last 10-25 letters of the first nine lines of a page or column.
Features: many superscript letters and suspension strokes (heavily abbreviated technical/scholastic-type writing - tentative interpretation); no rubric, no red, no enlarged initial, no underlining, no running title, no marginal note in the surviving margins. Lines 3-4 have wide internal spaces; one or two groups look inserted above the line (noted below). Whether the page had one or two columns cannot be seen.

TRANSCRIPTION (image-002; lines counted from the top of the image; all nine lines attempted)
Each line is a right-hand line end; "[...]" at the left marks loss by tearing. Superscript letters are shown with ^. Readings are tentative throughout; the hand is so compressed that most groups are abbreviations of two or three strokes.

image-002 line 1: [...] eadē(?) s(?)i d'e(?) pᵘt(?) d'(?) p^o(?) c^i(?) m^a(?)
        notes: first group may be "eade(m)" or "cade(n)s"; then a short group with a dot/stroke ("s. i." or "si"), "d'e"/"de"; "put"/"pat" with superscript (perhaps "p(ro)ut" or "p(ate)t"); then three very short suspended groups each with a superscript vowel.
image-002 line 2: [.]t(?) p^i a(?)  op^o(?)  [space]  p(?) .  Rz(?) q^r(?) sc(?)
        notes: "p" with superscript i then "a" (perhaps "p(ri)ma"); "op" with superscript o and a long descending flourish beneath; after a space "p" + suspension; then a group like "Rz"/"hz" (an R or h with a z-shaped sign), "qr"/"q(uia)" with superscript, and "sc"/"se" at the line end.
image-002 line 3: [.]g(?) disticcōs(?) cōpssi^ōis(?)   [wide space]   h(?) cu(?)
        notes: line opens with a g- or x-like sign joined by a long stroke from line 2; "disti..." (minims after -st-, ending in a suspension; "distinctio-" type word, ending unclear); second word begins "co"/"cō" or "ad", contains "p" or long s doubled, and ends in a superscript group "^nis"/"^ois". The final "h cu"/"h̄ eu" is written lower, between lines 3 and 4, with a superscript stroke: possibly an insertion or the end of line 3 dropped down.
image-002 line 4: f^a(?) mag(?) [space] a(?)cc̄t(?) [space] cū(?) istu(?)
        notes: "f" with superscript a (e.g. "f(orm)a"/"f(als)a" - not decidable); "mag" with a hooked suspension below the g (or "uig", "mcz"); a group under a long arched stroke, "accet"/"acat"/"agat"; "cū"/"au" with a stroke; final "istu"/"ista"/"iscu".
image-002 line 5: 7(?) [hole] [..]ēt(?) p^ricuic(?) accō(?)
        notes: tironian-et-like sign at the left edge, then a hole; after the hole a group ending "-ēt"/"-et" or "-ē" (a stroke below at the left, under the hole, may belong to it); then a word of p + minims ("p(ri)ncipi-"/"p(ar)ticul-" type, unresolved); last word "accō"/"actō" with suspension stroke (perhaps "actio"/"accio").
image-002 line 6: [...loss...] hoz(?) 7 p^imu(?)
        notes: left half lost; "hoz"/"hec"/"nos" with a z-shaped final; tironian 7 with a long horizontal head; "p" + superscript i + minims and a tall final stroke ("p(ri)mu(m)"/"p(ri)ma").
image-002 line 7: [...loss...] ꝓ(?) cū^t(?) nō(?) cu(?)
        notes: a p with crossed/looped descender ("p(ro)"/"p(er)"), then "cu"/"ca" with a superscript stroke ("cau(s)a"?), "nō"/"n̄o"/"io" with a suspension, and "cu"/"cii" at the line end.
image-002 line 8: [...loss, abraded patch...] g^a(?) gn̄a(?)
        notes: remains of two or three lost letters on the abraded patch, then "g"/"q" with superscript a, and a final word "g" + suspension + "a" ("g(e)n(er)a", "gr(ati)a" or "q(ua)n(t)a" type - not decidable).
image-002 line 9: [...loss...] [..]o(?) [..]b(?) q̄u(?)
        notes: only the tops/fragments of three groups along the torn lower edge; a looped stroke at the far left, a tall "b"/"h"/"k"-like letter, and "qu"/"q̄n" at the end.

SELECTION AND WHAT REMAINS UNREAD
All nine surviving lines were attempted; nothing was skipped. The scrap carries no span of ten lines. The other face is not in the packet and is therefore unread - a view of the reverse is the most useful addition to request, since it should carry the line beginnings of the neighbouring column or the verso.
Confidence is low overall. The comparatively firmer letter groups are: "disti...-" at the start of line 3 (after the opening sign), "mag-" and "ist-" in line 4, the tironian 7 followed by "p^i mu-" in line 6, and "nō" in line 7. None of the lines yields a securely read sequence of three words, so a source match would have to rest on the pattern of abbreviations rather than on quoted wording.

LIMITATIONS
- Line ends only; the left half or more of every line is lost, and the amount lost is unknown.
- Extremely abbreviated cursive: most groups are two or three letters plus superscripts, which admit several expansions; I have not chosen between expansions where the image does not decide.
- Holes in lines 2, 5-6 and 8-9; abraded whitish patch in line 8.
- Image resolution is good; the limits are the script and the losses, not the photograph.
- Unverified image reading.
